oneLiner: Closed at 28,957.53 Friday, little changed on the day and down about 0.8% on the week, roughly 7.3% below the record close of 31,224.47 set on October 6.
intro: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 28,957.53 on Friday, October 23, little changed on the day and down about 0.8% on the week, roughly 7.3% below its October 6 record close of 31,224.47. A 2.90% drop on Thursday, as doubts about AI spending hit chip stocks and Meta, erased a strong start to the week. Oil prices also climbed.

performance.heading: How the index has done
performance.body: The strip above tracks QQQ, the ETF that follows the Nasdaq-100, through the same week. The index rose on Monday and Wednesday, slipped a little on Tuesday, fell 2.90% on Thursday and finished Friday close to flat. The longer-period cards show how this second weekly loss in a row sits against the longer trend.

chart.heading: The trend against its moving averages
chart.body: The daily chart above plots QQQ against its 50- and 200-day moving averages. After Thursday's drop, the chart may show how close price sits to those lines and whether the slide from the October 6 record has paused or is still extending.

levels.heading: Where the nearby levels sit
levels.body: The week's highest close for the index was 29,822.52 on Wednesday, October 21. The October 6 record close of 31,224.47 sits further up, with Friday's close about 7.3% below it. The Price zones and Key levels cards above show where the nearby levels sit on QQQ today.

signals.heading: Momentum in plain words
signals.body: Momentum may look strained after a second weekly loss in a row and Thursday's 2.90% drop, which was led by chip stocks. The Nasdaq-100 was flat on Friday even as the S&P 500 and Dow fell, which may show pressure on the index easing, though one quiet day settles little. The panel above shows today's RSI and MACD readings on QQQ, which can differ from the index.

change.heading: The weekly and monthly pattern
change.body: Close to close, the index fell about 0.8% this week, after a 5.49% slide the week before, and was almost unchanged on Friday. It rose 1.17% on Monday, slipped 0.13% on Tuesday, gained 1.13% on Wednesday and fell 2.90% on Thursday. The tabs above show the daily, weekly and monthly changes on QQQ.

marketRead: The Nasdaq-100 ended the week at 28,957.53, down about 0.8% and roughly 7.3% below its October 6 record close of 31,224.47. It was a two-way week. The index gained 1.17% on Monday, October 19, and 1.13% on Wednesday, October 21, but Thursday, October 22 undid that with a 2.90% drop as worries about AI spending hit chip stocks, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down about 6.7%. Meta fell sharply after its results, with investors focused on its rising capital spending plans and its first negative free cash flow in over a decade.

Oil and rates framed the backdrop. Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel on Friday, its highest since late April, as Houthi attacks on Saudi targets, including energy infrastructure, and fears of escalation in the Iran war added to Middle East tension. U.S. crude closed near $103. The 10-year Treasury yield fell by about 11 basis points over the week and closed Friday just under 5%, edging up on the day. The Fed meets October 27-28 and is widely expected to hold rates, though Reuters reported futures priced roughly an 80% chance of a rate rise in December, after the Fed's September increase.

We could not confirm a dated figure for the share of Nasdaq-100 members above their 200-day average, so none is shown. The optimistic case is that the 10-year yield has stayed close to or below 5% and that Friday's flat finish may show the index finding a footing after Thursday's drop. The cautious case is that investors are questioning how AI spending will pay back, while high oil prices and a December rate rise that futures price at about 80% could keep pressure on growth valuations.

The coming weeks may hinge on results from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon next week, when capital spending plans will be watched closely, and on the Fed's meeting. Oil prices and any further moves in chip stocks may also shape how the index trades.

points.label: Catalyst
points.text: A 2.90% drop on Thursday as AI-spending worries hit chip stocks and Meta; Friday was little changed.

points.label: Record
points.text: The index set a record close of 31,224.47 on October 6; Friday's close sits about 7.3% below it.

points.label: Rates
points.text: The 10-year yield closed just under 5% on Friday, and Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel.

watchDown: Worries about AI spending spread from chip stocks to other large technology names.
Oil prices and Treasury yields climb further, pressing on growth company valuations.
Results from Microsoft, Alphabet or Amazon next week deepen the questions about AI spending.
The Fed's October 27-28 meeting brings a more cautious tone on inflation than investors expect.
watchUp: Chip stocks steady after Thursday's sharp drop and the Nasdaq-100's flat Friday.
Results from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon next week ease the questions about AI returns.
Oil prices ease and the 10-year yield stays close to or below 5%.
The index recovers toward its October 6 record close of 31,224.47.
